assessment.headline: Day 29. India is now in the crisis, not watching it. Excise slashed. Rupee at ATL. LPG choking. RBI burning reserves.
assessment.body:
India is no longer observing this war from a distance — it is IN the crisis. The government cut excise duty by ₹10/L and likened the situation to COVID. The rupee crashed to 94.79 — an all-time low. RBI has deployed $12-15 billion from forex reserves. Reserves fell $19 billion in two weeks. The Indian crude basket is at $125/barrel. Macquarie puts the probability of $200 oil at 40%.

91% of India's LPG comes from the Gulf — that supply is choked. 75% of the food service industry depends on LPG, costing ₹1,200-1,300 crore per day in losses. The government has invoked the Essential Commodities Act, imposed a 25-day LPG refill gap, capped industrial gas use, and is diverting all propane/butane to cooking gas. BPCL launched an LPG ATM. Oil companies are exploring 10kg cylinders.

The Christian Science Monitor called India 'the biggest loser in a war it isn't even fighting.' Pakistan has emerged as the key mediator while India is absent from diplomatic channels. The opposition accuses Modi of 'weakening India's neutrality.' EPW says India's strategic autonomy has been 'squandered in subservience to Western interests.'

Markets: Sensex at 73,583 — 5th straight weekly fall. FII outflow $11 billion in March. ₹44 lakh crore destroyed. Houthis have joined the war. Iran turned back ships from Hormuz. Brent is back at $110. April 6 is 9 days away. If talks fail, India faces the worst energy and economic crisis since independence — this is no longer hypothetical.
